more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Karaya gum is a dried tree exudate containing acetylated polysaccharides, mainly from Sterculia or Cochlospermum species. Its emulsifying role is to help form or maintain mixtures of oil and water in the finished food. Collected as dried gum exudate from suitable Sterculia or Cochlospermum species. It contains acetylated plant polysaccharides. The specified material is supplied as yellow powder or crystalline material.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; sauces; potato-, cereal-, flour- or starch-based snacks; processed nuts.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.origin: Collected as dried gum exudate from suitable Sterculia or Cochlospermum species. It contains acetylated plant polysaccharides.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specified starting material is plant derived and compatible with vegetarian and vegan diets. The specification does not establish halal or kosher certification.
